label: drop DEKs (REST action)
type: a REST-only operation that forces every DEK for a bucket or data type to be replaced, and with it forces the affected data to be re-encrypted - or, where encryption has been turned off, forces the decryption to actually happen rather than waiting for background re-write. Explicitly not the same as rotating DEKs.
evidence: You can force the decryption of data by calling the REST API to drop the DEKs for a bucket or type of data.
Dropping DEKs is not the same as rotating DEKs.
When you drop the DEKs for a bucket or type of data, Couchbase Server creates a new replacement DEK.
note: An id naming an ACTION available on only one surface. Filed because the fact that matters is exactly the surface restriction: disabling encryption at rest does not decrypt anything promptly, and the only documented way to make it do so is a REST call with no UI or CLI equivalent. Three cert: REST actions found in the same scope (load-trusted-cas, reload-certificate, regenerate-certificates) all sit at recurrence 1 and are refused, so the pattern is not being promoted wholesale.
